Let $M$ be a finite monoid and $p$ a prime. If $H_k(M;\F_p)=0$ for all sufficiently large $k$, then the order of $U(M)$ is prime to $p$. In particular, if the homology of $M$ is bounded, then $U(M)$ is trivial.

For a finite monoid $M$ the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{itemize} \item[\textup{(i)}] $BM$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex; \item[\textup{(ii)}] $BM$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-dimensional CW complex; \item[\textup{(iii)}] the homology of $M$ is bounded. \end{itemize} If they hold, $BM$ is simply connected.

Ben-Bassat {\cite[Theorem~C]{BB}}: Every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to $BM$ for some finite monoid $M$, which can be chosen aperiodic \textup{(}every $m\in M$ satisfies $m^{r+1}=m^r$ for some $r$\textup{)}.

\textup{(a)} A connected finite CW complex is homotopy equivalent to $BM$ for some finite monoid $M$ if and only if it is simply connected. \textup{(b)} Up to homotopy equivalence, the spaces $BM$ for finite monoids $M$ with bounded homology are exactly the finite simply connected CW complexes.

Conjecture~7.1 of \cite{BB}, ``Let $X$ be a connected finite CW complex. If $\pi_1(X)$ is finite, then $X\simeq BM$ for some finite monoid $M$'', is false. The real projective plane $\RP^2$ is a counterexample, and so is every connected finite CW complex whose fundamental group is finite and non-trivial.

Let $p$ be a prime, and let $X$ be a connected CW complex with finitely many cells in each dimension such that $H^q(X;\Zp)=0$ for all $q>n$, where $\Zp$ is the ring of rational numbers with denominator prime to $p$. Let $G$ be a finite group, $f\colon BG\to X$ a map, and $\rho\colon\pi_1(X)\to\GL_d(\CC)$ a homomorphism. Then $\rho(f_*(g))=1$ for every element $g\in G$ whose order is a power of $p$.

Let $X$ be a connected CW complex with finitely many cells in each dimension and with finite fundamental group, let $G$ be a finite group and $f\colon BG\to X$ a map. \textup{(a)} If $H^q(X;\Zp)=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$, then the order of $f_*(G)$ is prime to $p$. \textup{(b)} If $H^q(X;\Z)=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$, then $f_*$ is trivial.

Let $M$ be a finite monoid. \textup{(a)} $\pi_1(BM)\cong U(M)$, the loop formed by the $1$-cell $(m)$ corresponding to $\eta(m)$. \textup{(b)} $\eta\colon M\to U(M)$ is surjective and $U(M)$ is finite. \textup{(c)} Let $e$ be an idempotent of the minimal two-sided ideal of $M$. Then $H=eMe$ is a finite group with identity $e$, and $\eta$ restricts to a surjective homomorphism of groups $H\to U(M)$.
With $e$ and $H$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:known}\,\textup{(c)}, there is a map $j_e\colon BH\to BM$ whose effect on fundamental groups is $\eta|_H\colon H\to U(M)$, up to an inner automorphism.

Let $M$ be a finite monoid such that the trivial left \textup{(}or right\textup{)} $\Z M$-module $\Z$ has a projective resolution of finite length. Then the group $H=eMe$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:known}\,\textup{(c)} is trivial. In particular $U(M)$ is trivial, and $BM$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite simply connected CW complex.

\textup{(a)} $U(M_6)$ is trivial. \textup{(b)} $H_0(M_6;\Z)=\Z$, $H_1(M_6;\Z)=0$ and $H_n(M_6;\Z)\cong\Z$ for every $n\ge2$. \textup{(c)} $BM_6$ is homotopy equivalent to the wedge $\bigvee_{n\ge2}S^n$ of one sphere of each dimension $n\ge2$.

The set $M_{23}$ is closed under the product; it is an aperiodic monoid with $23$ elements. The trivial left $\Z M_{23}$-module has a projective resolution of length $4$, the groups $H_k(M_{23};\Z)$ are $\Z$ for $k=0,2,4$ and zero otherwise, and $BM_{23}$ is homotopy equivalent to $\CP^2$.
